one_liner: x86/x86-64 JIT plug-in for AngelScript 2.31.0 that turns bytecode into native code; about 1.10x over the interpreter on scriptorium fib(34).
what_it_does: Implements AngelScript's asIJITCompiler interface: you create an asCJITCompiler(flags), set asEP_INCLUDE_JIT_INSTRUCTIONS, call engine->SetJITCompiler(jit), and every script function built afterwards gets native x86 or x86-64 code; bytecodes it cannot handle hand control back to the normal VM. Scripts, host bindings and the engine API stay unchanged, so it is an add-on to the stock AngelScript SDK rather than a different engine. Optional finalizePages() makes the code pages read-only after loading.
how_it_is_fast: A template (one-pass) JIT: as_jit.cpp walks each function's bytecode and emits machine code per opcode through its own small assembler (virtual_asm_x86.cpp / virtual_asm_x64.cpp), removing the interpreter's dispatch loop and register-file loads and stores. Script-to-script calls are made natively (JitScriptCall) instead of returning to the VM, switch statements become native jump tables, and system calls are emitted inline per calling convention. Build flags (JIT_NO_SUSPEND, JIT_SYSCALL_NO_ERRORS, JIT_ALLOC_SIMPLE, JIT_FAST_REFCOUNT, JIT_SYSCALL_FPU_NORESET) drop suspend checks, exception checks and context bookkeeping for more speed.
when_to_use: You already ship an AngelScript 2.29-2.31 host on Windows (MSVC 2010+) or Linux (GCC 4.6.2+) and want extra speed without changing scripts or bindings.
Hot script code is arithmetic, branches and script-to-script calls; those opcodes are compiled natively and do not fall back to the VM.
You can live without line callbacks and context suspension in hot code and build with JIT_NO_SUSPEND; scriptorium built with flags 0 and a per-line callback and saw only about 10 percent.
32-bit x86 targets: angelsea, the newer AngelScript JIT, explicitly does not support 32-bit x86 and points users here.
when_not_to_use: AngelScript 2.32 or newer: the JIT reads VM internals (asCContext and asSVMRegisters offsets) and was last updated for 2.31.0 in February 2016; issue #29 (2023) asking for newer versions is unanswered.
ARM, Apple Silicon or any non-x86 target: x86 and x86-64 only (issue #6 asking for ARM is open since 2014).
When you need a large speed-up on a measured benchmark: the only third-party number is about 1.10x on fib(34), and the JIT's own README gives no performance figures.

Hosts that rely on native calls with const-reference arguments returning objects on the stack on x86-64: open issue #27 (2022, AngelScript 2.35.1, MSVC) reports call_64conv clobbering an argument with the return value; open issues #17 (formatInt crash) and #23 (random crash) are also unresolved.
Projects that need a maintained dependency: last commit 2016-06-28, no maintainer replies since.

integration.dependencies: AngelScript SDK 2.31.0 sources (needs the internal headers, not only angelscript.h); no other libraries
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (lambdas, auto); MSVC 2010+ or GCC 4.6.2+ with -std=c++11
integration.platforms: x86 and x86-64 on Windows (virtual_asm_windows.cpp) and Linux (virtual_asm_linux.cpp); no ARM
integration.thread_safety: README: the JIT is thread-safe, one asCJITCompiler can serve several engines and several engines can compile at once (compilation is guarded by a CriticalSection).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — scripts and bindings are unchanged and unsupported bytecodes fall back to the interpreter, but it only works with the AngelScript versions it was written for (2.31.0 in master, 2.29.x in older commits) and the speed flags change error and suspend semantics

gotchas: Harness flaw behind the 1.10x: scriptorium's angelscript/main.cpp (shared by as.exe and asjit.exe) installs ctx->SetLineCallback with a timeout check that calls timeGetTime() on every script statement, and builds the JIT with asCJITCompiler(0). With a line callback set, the vendored as_jit.cpp emits an out-of-line call to doSuspend, which calls CallLineCallback, at every asBC_SUSPEND, so both builds pay a host callback per statement; fib(34) runs fibR 18,454,929 times (derived), each executing at least two statements. This fixed cost is the same in both builds and compresses the measured ratio; the JIT's speed with JIT_NO_SUSPEND and no line callback was never measured.

Other harness limits: whole-process wall time including engine setup, compile and JIT compile (bench.cc runs the exe 5 times via system() and divides), script output never checked; the README table shows the minimum per name across bench.csv sessions (JIT 1.879/1.956/1.859 s, interpreter 2.046/2.081/2.039 s), and the Lua reference row comes from a different session (2.359 s in session 1, 1.341 s later), so the 72 percent relative-Lua column mixes sessions.

Measured code is the December 2014 snapshot vendored in scriptorium with AngelScript 2.29.2; 2016 fixes followed for sub-line jumps broken by multi-bytecode optimizations, suspends returning to the VM at the wrong instruction, asBC_POW using wrong registers on 64-bit, and asCALL_CDECL_OBJLAST clobbering the stack for 4+ parameters. None is on fib's path as far as the code shows.

JIT_SYSCALL_NO_ERRORS and JIT_FAST_REFCOUNT are unsafe if any registered function sets a script exception or inspects the context (README: 'will likely result in crashes'); asBC_DIVd has a TODO about not raising AngelScript's divide-by-zero error.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it only when you are locked into AngelScript 2.31 on x86; among siblings in the same scriptorium table, LuaJIT-class or compiled options (Terra 0.121 s, c4x86 0.136 s, Pawn 0.384 s) and even PUC Lua (1.341 s) beat its 1.859 s on fib(34), so a new project wanting a fast embedded language should look at Luau, LuaJIT Remake or Daslang instead.
verified_claims_summary: Third-party scriptorium suite (r-lyeh, 2015, Windows 7 x64, AMD A10 3.8 GHz, MSVC 2015 RC or 2013 with /Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG): recursive fib(34) script, whole process averaged over 5 runs, took 1.859 s with this JIT (AngelScript 2.29.2, flags 0) versus 2.039 s for the same host without it, about 1.10x (derived from page data), with a per-statement line callback active in both builds.
status_note: Abandoned since June 2016 (5 open issues, 2 open pull requests, no maintainer activity) but MIT-licensed and eight source files, so it can be vendored for AngelScript 2.31.0 on x86/x86-64; for AngelScript 2.37+ on x86-64 the angelsea project (AsuMagic/angelsea, MIR-based) claims 0 to 40 percent more than this JIT in a real application.
